title: ASPIRe: the SFC's virtual-asset roadmap
md:
The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) published ASPIRe in February 2025. It is a roadmap of five pillars and 12 initiatives for Hong Kong's virtual-asset (VA) market. [S:cfe8a53186c3, para 1] Some roadmap items, such as VA financing, now reach banks through Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) guidance. [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.2, 'HKMA's guidance for RIs', items (1)-(2)] ASPIRe's licensing work also led to planned regimes under which banks would register with the SFC. [S:d461c2db6af2, Pillar A, Initiative 1]; [S:7395a53cc85a, para 4]

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Run by | SFC [S:cfe8a53186c3, para 1] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | Exploratory (roadmap); several initiatives since delivered through SFC circulars and guidance [S:36753b22e10a, para 2]; [S:f09e57feb89b, paras 2, 4]; [S:089ec86e2407, para 2] |
| Started | 19 Feb 2025 [S:cfe8a53186c3, para 1] |
| Next official date | H2 2026: SFC digital-asset custody surveillance system to begin operating (stated target in the Policy Address) [S:ef3648ff1610, para 51(iii)] |
| Covered in | [A3](#m-A3), [C1](#m-C1), [C3](#m-C3), [C6](#m-C6), [C7](#m-C7), [E1](#m-E1) |
## What it is

ASPIRe stands for five pillars: Access, Safeguards, Products, Infrastructure and Relationships. Together they hold 12 initiatives. [S:cfe8a53186c3, para 1]

- **Access** covers new licensing regimes for over-the-counter (OTC) VA dealing and for VA custody. OTC deals are agreed directly between two parties, not on an exchange. [S:d461c2db6af2, Pillar A, Initiative 1] ASPIRe says the government-led work to prepare the law for custodians aimed to finish by end-2025. [S:d461c2db6af2, Pillar A, Initiative 1]
- **Safeguards** includes exploring custody standards that focus on results and do not favour any one technology. [S:d461c2db6af2, Pillar S, Initiative 3] It also includes a more flexible approach to cold-storage ratios, meaning the share of client assets kept offline. [S:d461c2db6af2, Pillar S, Initiative 3]
- **Products** looks at: [S:d461c2db6af2, Pillar P, Initiatives 6-8]
  - new token listings
  - derivatives (contracts whose value tracks another asset) for professional investors
  - margin financing (lending to clients so they can buy assets)
  - staking (locking up tokens to help run a blockchain, for a reward)
  - borrowing and lending
- **Infrastructure** covers tools for regulatory reporting and surveillance. One example is wallet tracing, which follows tokens as they move between wallets. [S:d461c2db6af2, Pillar I, Initiative 9]

The SFC frames many initiatives as things it will explore or consider. [S:d461c2db6af2, Initiatives 3, 6-9, 11]

## Timeline

| Date | Milestone | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 19 Feb 2025 | ASPIRe roadmap published | Exploratory | [S:cfe8a53186c3, para 1] |
| 7 Apr 2025 | Staking guidance for VA trading platforms (VATPs) and VA funds, framed under Pillar P | In force | [S:36753b22e10a, para 2, Note 2] |
| 27 Jun 2025 | VA dealing and custodian consultations (Pillar A); conclusions published 24 Dec 2025 | Conclusions published | [S:7395a53cc85a, para 1]; [S:6186c01c6649, Introduction, p.3 and fn 2] |
| 15 Aug 2025 | SFC custody circular to VATPs cites Pillar S, Initiative 3 | In force | [S:562c0f8addce, 'Importance of resilient custody controls and expected standards' section, p.1] |
| 3 Nov 2025 | Circulars on shared order books and on a wider product range (Pillars A and P) | In force | [S:f09e57feb89b, paras 2, 4] |
| 11 Feb 2026 | VA financing, a framework for perpetual contracts, and platforms' own affiliates acting as market makers | Issued | [S:089ec86e2407, paras 1-4] |
| H2 2026 | SFC digital-asset custody surveillance system to begin operating | Stated target | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 51(iii)] |
| 2027 | Parts of CrypTech (an SFC initiative) that use big data for market and anti-money laundering surveillance | Stated target | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 51(iii)] |

## What it means for your bank

- The SFC calls the roadmap a plan that will keep changing, not a final destination. [S:cfe8a53186c3, para 5] Its initiatives take effect through separate circulars (SFC letters to firms) and guidance. Examples include the circulars on staking and VA financing. [S:36753b22e10a, paras 2-3]; [S:089ec86e2407, para 2]
- VA financing now reaches banks too. [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.2, 'HKMA's guidance for RIs', items (1)-(2)] Registered institutions (RIs) are banks registered with the SFC. RIs that provide VA dealing services may lend to their securities margin clients for VA dealing. Margin clients are clients who borrow from the firm to invest. [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.2, 'HKMA's guidance for RIs', items (1)-(2)] The HKMA expects these RIs to observe standards similar to the SFC's. [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.2, 'HKMA's guidance for RIs', items (1)-(2)]
- Licensed and registered firms, including RIs, may offer staking to clients for whom they deal in virtual assets. [S:d5ebca32c92b, paras 4-5] They should use only segregated accounts, kept apart from the firm's own assets. [S:d5ebca32c92b, paras 4-5] Those accounts should sit at an SFC-licensed platform or at an authorized financial institution. [S:d5ebca32c92b, paras 4-5]
- The SFC's framework covers perpetual contracts on VATPs. These are derivatives with no expiry date. VATPs should offer them only to professional investors. [S:49f642bdee28, 'Eligible investors and reference assets'; 'Margin arrangements and loss allocation management'] Margin collateral is what clients post to back their trades. It should be fiat money (ordinary currency), or stablecoins or tokenised deposits regulated by the HKMA. [S:49f642bdee28, 'Eligible investors and reference assets'; 'Margin arrangements and loss allocation management']
- Pillar A's plans for OTC trading and custody became the proposed VA dealing and custodian regimes. Banks would register rather than be licensed, with the HKMA as frontline regulator. [S:d461c2db6af2, Pillar A, Initiative 1]; [S:7395a53cc85a, para 4] Two further proposed regimes cover VA advisory and VA management. Under those regimes too, only banks could register with the SFC. [S:6186c01c6649, paras 52, 58 and fns 9-10]

## Talking points

- **To the CCO:** ASPIRe is a roadmap. Its initiatives take effect through separate SFC circulars and guidance, so track those. [S:cfe8a53186c3, para 5]; [S:089ec86e2407, para 2]
- **To business heads:** Items delivered so far include staking, shared order books, VA financing and perpetual contracts for professional investors. [S:36753b22e10a, para 2]; [S:f09e57feb89b, para 2]; [S:089ec86e2407, paras 2-3]
- **To the CEO:** The SFC's Executive Director of Intermediaries called the roadmap-based approach essential to scaling Hong Kong's digital asset market. [S:089ec86e2407, para 5]
- **To Risk:** The SFC still frames custody standards based on results as something to explore. [S:d461c2db6af2, Pillar S, Initiative 3] But its August 2025 custody circular to VATPs took effect immediately. [S:562c0f8addce, 'Way forward', p.7]

"A-S-P-I-Re" for a brighter future: SFC's regulatory roadmap for Hong Kong's virtual asset market — SFC — 19 Feb 2025 — read all five pillar sections — https://www.sfc.hk/en/News-and-announcements/Policy-statements-and-announcements/A-S-P-I-Re-for-a-brighter-future-SFCs-regulatory-roadmap-for-Hong-Kongs-virtual-asset-market
2. SFC sets out new roadmap to develop Hong Kong as a global virtual asset hub — SFC — 19 Feb 2025 — read paras 1-3 — https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/gateway/EN/news-and-announcements/news/doc?refNo=25PR20
3. SFC launches trading initiatives to boost digital asset market vibrancy in Hong Kong — SFC — 11 Feb 2026 — read paras 2-4 — https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/gateway/EN/news-and-announcements/news/doc?refNo=26PR24
4. The Chief Executive's 2026 Policy Address — Hong Kong Government — 16 Sep 2026 — read paras 49 and 51(iii) — https://www.policyaddress.gov.hk/2026/public/pdf/policy/policy-full_en.pdf

title: Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF) and amended CRS
md:
A Hong Kong bill would update the Common Reporting Standard (CRS) and bring in the Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF). [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview] Since 2018, Hong Kong has used the CRS to exchange financial account information with other tax authorities each year. [S:252a7f86684e, paras 2-4] CARF is a yearly crypto-asset tax reporting standard from the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD). [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview] Why banks care: a group entity offering crypto exchange services to customers as a business can become a reporting crypto-asset service provider (RCASP). [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50M] If the bill passes, CARF duties start on 1 January 2027. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(3)]

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Run by | Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau (FSTB) and Inland Revenue Department (IRD) [S:275d5cc93a88, Foreword, para 1] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | Bill before LegCo (the Legislative Council, Hong Kong's law-making body). Gazetted (published in the official Gazette) 22 May 2026. First and Second Readings (formal introduction) set for 3 Jun 2026, with the Second Reading debate adjourned. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview] |
| Started | Commitment to the OECD Global Forum, 13 Dec 2024 [S:ea81f92ea327, para 1] |
| Next official date | 1 Jan 2027: CARF duties start, if the bill passes [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(3)] |
| Covered in | [D5](#m-D5), [A3](#m-A3), [E1](#m-E1), [E3](#m-E3) |
## What it is

CARF is an OECD standard. Under it, jurisdictions automatically exchange crypto-asset tax information each year. [S:ea81f92ea327, para 2] Hong Kong aimed to have its law in place by 2026 and to start exchanges from 2028. [S:ea81f92ea327, para 4]

Under the bill, an RCASP is a person that, as a business, carries out crypto exchange transactions for customers. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50M "reporting crypto-asset service provider"] This includes acting as a counterparty (the other side of a trade) or an intermediary, or running a trading platform. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50M "reporting crypto-asset service provider"]

An RCASP with a Hong Kong nexus (a close link to Hong Kong) would have to: [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, ss.50O-50Q, 50S]

- register;
- carry out due diligence (checks on its customers);
- file returns (reports to the tax authority);
- keep records.

Central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) and specified e-money products are outside CARF. [S:275d5cc93a88, paras 1.5, 4.3] The amended CRS brings them in instead. [S:275d5cc93a88, paras 1.5, 4.3] If the bill passes, CARF starts on 1 January 2027. The amended CRS starts on 1 January 2028. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(3)-(4)]

## Timeline

| Date | Milestone | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 13 Dec 2024 | Hong Kong commits to CARF; first exchanges from 2028 | Stated target | [S:ea81f92ea327, paras 1, 4] |
| 9 Dec 2025 | FSTB and IRD public consultation (open until 6 Feb 2026) | Superseded | [S:252a7f86684e, paras 1, 7]; [S:275d5cc93a88, Foreword, para 1] |
| 25 Feb 2026 | Budget: amendment bill in the first half of 2026 | Stated target | [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 108] |
| 22 May 2026 | Bill gazetted | Bill before LegCo | [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview] |
| 3 Jun 2026 | First and Second Readings; Second Reading debate (on the bill's main principles) adjourned | Bill before LegCo | [S:d5097f447cf9, para 1]; [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview] |
| 1 Jan 2027 | Part 2 (CARF) starts, if passed | Bill before LegCo | [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(3)] |
| 1 Jan 2028 | Part 3 (amended CRS) starts, if passed | Bill before LegCo | [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(4)] |

## What it means for your bank

- Under the bill, any group entity would be an RCASP if, as a business, it carries out crypto exchange transactions for customers. Acting as an intermediary counts. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50M]
- The Hong Kong nexus tests look at: [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50N(1)-(2)]
  - tax residence;
  - incorporation;
  - management;
  - a regular place of business;
  - Hong Kong branches.
- A Hong Kong RCASP would have to register by 31 January of the year after it first meets a nexus test. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50O(1)-(2)]
- An RCASP would need self-certifications of tax residence (customers' own statements of where they are tax resident) from new customers. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Due diligence requirements'] For existing users, the same applies within 12 months of the rules taking effect. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Due diligence requirements']
- Under the amended CRS, crypto-linked derivatives count as financial assets. [S:275d5cc93a88, paras 4.3-4.4] CBDCs and specified e-money products are added to the definition of a depository account (a deposit-type account). [S:275d5cc93a88, paras 4.3-4.4]
- Registration and returns would go to the IRD through its planned CARF Portal. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Reporting portal and mandatory registration requirement']
- Hiring a service provider would not, on its own, be a reasonable excuse (a legal defence). [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.80R(2)] This covers failing to register, do due diligence or file returns. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.80R(2)]

## Talking points

- **To the CCO:** The bill is not yet law. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview] If passed, CARF duties start on 1 January 2027 and amended CRS on 1 January 2028. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(3)-(4)]
- **To business heads:** A customer crypto exchange service run as a business can make the entity an RCASP. This applies even when the entity acts as an intermediary. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50M]
- **To the CEO:** Hong Kong committed to CARF in December 2024, with first data exchanges targeted from 2028. [S:ea81f92ea327, para 4]
- **To Risk:** Proposed fines can scale. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.80R(4)-(5)] Some continuing offences carry a further HK$500 a day after conviction. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.80R(4)-(5)] For due-diligence offences, the fine is the higher of two amounts: a level 3 fine, or HK$1,000 per affected user or controlling person. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.80R(4)-(5)] A level 3 fine is a set point on Hong Kong's scale of fines.

## Key documents

Inland Revenue (Amendment) (CARF and Amended CRS) Bill 2026 — LegCo / IRD — gazetted 22 May 2026 — read Clause 1, ss.50M-50R, 80R and 82E-82F — https://www.ird.gov.hk/eng/pdf/carf/Inland%20Revenue%20(Amendment)%20(Crypto-Asset%20Reporting%20Framework%20and%20Amended%20Common%20Reporting%20Standard)%20Bill%202026(eng).pdf
2. Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework page — IRD — undated — read the Overview, due diligence, registration and penalty sections — https://www.ird.gov.hk/eng/tax/dta_carf.htm
3. Implementation of CARF and Amendments in Relation to CRS (consultation paper) — FSTB and IRD — 9 Dec 2025 — read paras 4.3-4.18 and Chapter 6 — https://www.gov.hk/en/residents/government/publication/consultation/docs/2026/crypto-framework.pdf
4. Hong Kong commits to implementing Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework — FSTB — 13 Dec 2024 — read paras 1-4 — https://www.info.gov.hk/gia/general/202412/13/P2024121300491.htm

title: CBDC research and cross-border digital money pilots
md:
CBDC means central bank digital currency: money issued in digital form by a central bank. This page covers the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) research projects on CBDC and tokenised money (money recorded as digital tokens on a shared ledger). The projects are Aurum, Sela, Genesis and Inthanon-LionRock (a joint study with the Bank of Thailand). [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Collaborative Projects' and 'Project Inthanon-LionRock' sections] The page also covers the cross-boundary pilot of e-CNY (the Mainland's digital renminbi). [S:08caafe0cfe7, para 1] It also covers a 2026 memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Shanghai bodies. [S:eb28508e5032, para 1] Why it matters to your bank: 18 local banks in Hong Kong support top-ups of pilot e-CNY wallets. [S:062b0a1547b9, Reply (1)]

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Run by | HKMA, with the Bank for International Settlements Innovation Hub (BISIH), other central banks and Mainland bodies [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Collaborative Projects']; [S:08caafe0cfe7, para 1]; [S:eb28508e5032, para 1] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | Research (Aurum, Sela, Genesis); Pilot (e-CNY); Exploratory (Shanghai MoU) [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Collaborative Projects']; [S:062b0a1547b9, Reply (1)-(2)]; [S:eb28508e5032, paras 1-2] |
| Started | Q4 2019 (Inthanon-LionRock) [S:6b0fae230518, footnote 1] |
| Next official date | None stated. The plans to upgrade e-CNY wallets and raise limits have no final timetable. [S:062b0a1547b9, Reply (2)] |
| Covered in | [E2](#m-E2), [C5](#m-C5), [E3](#m-E3) |
## What it is

Project Aurum built a two-tier prototype with the BISIH and a local research institute. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Collaborative Projects'] It linked a wholesale system (for payments between banks) with retail e-wallets (for the public). [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Collaborative Projects'] Its report came out in October 2022. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Collaborative Projects']

The HKMA ran Project Sela with the Bank of Israel. [S:8146b4a87d45, paras 2 and 5] Sela tested whether non-bank firms, called Access Enablers, could connect directly to a central bank's CBDC ledger (the record of who holds what). [S:8146b4a87d45, paras 2 and 5] Sela's report says it reflects no HKMA policy decision on a possible e-HKD (a digital Hong Kong dollar). [S:f9000467b0ee, Section 1, footnote 5, p.5]

Project Genesis built test platforms with the BISIH for tokenising green bonds (issuing them as digital tokens). [S:5a9cad53f2be, footnote 4] Genesis ended in 2021. The Government's 2023 tokenised green bond built on its work. [S:a0841967c871, quote from Eddie Yue]

Inthanon-LionRock studied CBDC for cross-border payments with the Bank of Thailand. It later grew into mBridge. [S:6b0fae230518, para 1 and footnote 1]

The cross-boundary e-CNY pilot lets Hong Kong residents open personal e-CNY wallets with a Hong Kong mobile number. [S:08caafe0cfe7, paras 1-2; Annex 1] They top up the wallets through the Faster Payment System (FPS), Hong Kong's instant payment system. [S:08caafe0cfe7, paras 1-2; Annex 1]

## Timeline

| Date | Milestone | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q4 2019 | Inthanon-LionRock starts with the Bank of Thailand | Superseded | [S:6b0fae230518, footnote 1] |
| 2021 | Project Genesis ends | Research | [S:a0841967c871, quote from Eddie Yue] |
| Oct 2022 | Project Aurum report | Research | [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Collaborative Projects'] |
| 12 Sep 2023 | Project Sela report | Research | [S:8146b4a87d45, paras 1-2] |
| 20 Oct 2023 | HKMA sets up a CBDC Expert Group with five local universities | Research | [S:28af6d5e86cb, para 1] |
| 17 May 2024 | Cross-boundary e-CNY pilot widened | Pilot | [S:08caafe0cfe7, para 1] |
| 8 Oct 2025 | Government says the e-CNY wallet upgrade is still under discussion | Pilot | [S:2ffb8727bb2f, Reply (3) and (5)] |
| 2 Mar 2026 | HKMA, Shanghai Data Bureau and a national blockchain centre sign an MoU on digital cargo trade and trade finance | Exploratory | [S:eb28508e5032, paras 1-2] |
| 25 Mar 2026 | Government reports about 80,000 e-CNY wallets and 18 top-up banks | Pilot | [S:062b0a1547b9, Reply (1)] |

## What it means for your bank

- Sela's report says the project reflects no HKMA policy decision on a possible e-HKD. [S:f9000467b0ee, Section 1, footnote 5, p.5]
- Pilot wallets are "tier-4" personal wallets. Their limits, in Chinese renminbi (RMB), are:
  - RMB 10,000 balance;
  - RMB 2,000 per transaction;
  - RMB 5,000 a day;
  - RMB 50,000 a year. [S:08caafe0cfe7, Annex 2, pp.1-2]
- Pilot wallets do not allow person-to-person transfers. Operating institutions may set lower limits. [S:08caafe0cfe7, Annex 2, pp.1-2]
- 18 local banks in Hong Kong support FPS top-ups. [S:062b0a1547b9, Reply (1)-(2)] The People's Bank of China (PBoC) and the HKMA are exploring wallet upgrades to raise limits. The proposals and timing are not final. [S:062b0a1547b9, Reply (1)-(2)]
- The Shanghai MoU says the parties will explore cross-border financial cooperation and electronic bills of lading (digital shipping documents) under Project Ensemble. [S:eb28508e5032, para 2] They will also study trade finance that uses cargo and trade data from linked data platforms. [S:eb28508e5032, para 2]
- The Government says stablecoins, CBDC such as e-CNY, and tokenised deposits each have their own features and maturity. It says market forces will largely decide their future. [S:062b0a1547b9, Reply (3)]

## Talking points

- **To the CCO:** Sela and Aurum were research projects. Sela's report says it reflects no HKMA policy decision on an e-HKD. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Collaborative Projects'; S:f9000467b0ee, Section 1, footnote 5, p.5]
- **To business heads:** About 80,000 e-CNY wallets were registered by end-January 2026. 18 Hong Kong banks support FPS top-ups. [S:062b0a1547b9, Reply (1)]
- **To the CEO:** Under the 2026 Shanghai MoU, the parties will explore electronic bills of lading under Project Ensemble. [S:eb28508e5032, para 2]
- **To Risk:** Pilot e-CNY wallets do not allow person-to-person transfers. They cap balances at RMB 10,000. [S:08caafe0cfe7, Annex 2, pp.1-2]

3. Expanding the cross-boundary e-CNY pilot in Hong Kong — HKMA — 17 May 2024 — read paras 1-2 and Annexes 1-2 — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/news-and-media/press-releases/2024/05/20240517-3/

Hong Kong Monetary Authority, Shanghai Data Bureau, and National Technology Innovation Center for Blockchain sign MoU to strengthen Shanghai-Hong Kong cooperation in digitised cargo trade and finance — HKMA — 2 Mar 2026 — read paras 1-2 — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/news-and-media/press-releases/2026/03/20260302-3/

title: CMU OmniClear digital asset platform and tokenised Exchange Fund Bills
md:
CMU OmniClear (the company that runs Hong Kong's central bond settlement system) plans a digital asset platform. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii), (iv)] That system is the Central Moneymarkets Unit (CMU), Hong Kong's central securities depository. [S:9c8855ec55a1, para 2] A central securities depository is where bonds are held and settled. Separately, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) intends to test tokenised Exchange Fund Bills. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii), (iv)] "Tokenised" means recorded as digital tokens on a shared ledger. Exchange Fund Bills are short-term debt issued by the HKMA. Why banks care: the Policy Address links the bill tests to how banks manage their assets and liabilities. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii)] The platform is meant to be a one-stop service for issuing and settling digital bonds. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(iv)]

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Run by | CMU OmniClear Limited runs the CMU on behalf of the HKMA. The HKMA runs the Exchange Fund Bills tests. [S:d43a14fd959f, paras 1-3]; [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii)] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | Stated target [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii), (iv)] |
| Started | CMU OmniClear set up 18 Oct 2024 [S:d43a14fd959f, para 1] |
| Next official date | Platform: "this year" (2026). Exchange Fund Bills tests: by year-end 2026. Both are stated targets. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii), (iv)] |
| Covered in | [C5](#m-C5), [A3](#m-A3), [E1](#m-E1), [E3](#m-E3) |
## What it is

The HKMA set up CMU OmniClear to run the CMU under a contract with the HKMA. [S:d43a14fd959f, paras 1-2] At set-up, the Exchange Fund (Hong Kong's official reserves) wholly owned the company. [S:d43a14fd959f, paras 1-2] The HKMA stays the owner and system operator of the CMU. The HKMA also holds the legal relationships with CMU participants (the firms that use the CMU) and makes CMU policy decisions. [S:d43a14fd959f, para 3]; [S:9c8855ec55a1, para 6]

Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing (HKEX) is taking a 20% stake in the holding company, CMU OmniClear Holdings. The Exchange Fund keeps 80%. [S:9c8855ec55a1, para 2]

The 2026-27 Budget said CMU OmniClear would set up a digital asset platform in 2026, for issuing and settling digital bonds. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 114] The Budget said the platform would later cover other digital assets and link to other tokenisation platforms in the region. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 114]

The 2026 Policy Address repeats the platform target. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii), (iv)] It also says the HKMA will test tokenising Exchange Fund Bills by year-end. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii), (iv)] The purpose is to let banks use more than HK$1.3 trillion of these bills at any hour. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii), (iv)]

The Hong Kong Mortgage Corporation (HKMC) issued digital bonds in June 2026. [S:6aa27ee8b400, para 4] The bonds were created on a distributed ledger technology (DLT) platform run by the CMU. DLT is a shared digital record kept in step across many computers. [S:6aa27ee8b400, para 4] The CMU acted as the clearing and settlement system for these bonds. [S:6aa27ee8b400, para 4]

## Timeline

| Date | Milestone | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16 Feb 2023 | First tokenised Government bond clears through the CMU with statutory finality (settlement the law treats as final) | Issued | [S:a0841967c871, paras 1, 4] |
| 18 Oct 2024 | HKMA sets up CMU OmniClear Limited | In force | [S:d43a14fd959f, para 1] |
| 4 Mar 2025 | CMU OmniClear and HKEX sign a memorandum of understanding (MoU) on post-trade systems | Exploratory | [S:74db8f7570bd, paras 1-2] |
| 12 Nov 2025 | HKEX to take 20% of CMU OmniClear Holdings | Announced | [S:9c8855ec55a1, para 2] |
| 25 Feb 2026 | Budget: digital asset platform to be set up in 2026 | Stated target | [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 114] |
| 10 Jun 2026 | HKMC digital bonds priced; created on a DLT platform run by the CMU | Issued | [S:6aa27ee8b400, paras 1, 4] |
| 16 Sep 2026 | Policy Address: platform this year; tokenised Exchange Fund Bills tests by year-end | Stated target | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii), (iv)] |

## What it means for your bank

- Nothing is binding yet. Both items are stated targets. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii), (iv)] The sources reviewed show no platform rulebook and no test design. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii), (iv)]
- The Policy Address links the Exchange Fund Bills tests to how banks manage their assets and liabilities. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii)]
- The Digital Bond Grant Scheme is an HKMA subsidy for digital bond issues. Issuing on a DLT platform run by the CMU meets one of its two alternative Basic Requirements. [S:5a0563de8142, s.2 and fn 6, p.3] The HKMA decides case by case whether a platform counts. [S:5a0563de8142, s.2 and fn 6, p.3]
- The law treats the CMU as a designated clearing and settlement system. So its settlements have statutory finality. [S:a0b44be27c40, paras 36-38, pp.14-15] Another DLT platform gets statutory finality only if the HKMA designates it. Otherwise, the parties can agree on finality in their contract. [S:a0b44be27c40, paras 36-38, pp.14-15]
- The HKMA's February 2024 circular on tokenised products does not cover products regulated under the Securities and Futures Ordinance (the main securities law). [S:b2719f3dcb37, 'Coverage' and fn 2, p.1] Those products follow the relevant Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) and HKMA requirements. [S:b2719f3dcb37, 'Coverage' and fn 2, p.1]

## Talking points

- **To the CCO:** No rules are out yet for the platform or the Exchange Fund Bills tests. Both are stated targets. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii), (iv)]
- **To business heads:** The platform is meant to be a one-stop service for issuing and settling digital bonds. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(iv)]
- **To the CEO:** The HKMA plans tests of tokenised Exchange Fund Bills by end-2026. This is to help banks use more than HK$1.3 trillion of these bills round the clock. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii)]
- **To Risk:** A DLT platform has statutory finality only if the HKMA designates it. Otherwise, finality rests on contract. [S:a0b44be27c40, paras 37-38, p.15]

## Key documents

1. The Chief Executive's 2026 Policy Address — Hong Kong Government — 16 Sep 2026 — read para 35 (pp.22-23) — https://www.policyaddress.gov.hk/2026/public/pdf/policy/policy-full_en.pdf
2. 2026-27 Budget — Financial Secretary — 25 Feb 2026 — read paras 112-114 — https://www.budget.gov.hk/2026/eng/pdf/e_budget_speech_2026-27.pdf
3. HKMA Establishes CMU OmniClear Limited — HKMA — 18 Oct 2024 — read paras 1-3 — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/news-and-media/press-releases/2024/10/20241018-5/
4. HKMA introduces HKEX as a strategic shareholder in CMU OmniClear Holdings Limited — HKMA — 12 Nov 2025 — read paras 2 and 6 — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/news-and-media/press-releases/2025/11/20251112-3/

title: Digital Bond Grant Scheme (DBGS)
md:
The Digital Bond Grant Scheme (DBGS) is a subsidy from the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA). It refunds part of the cost of issuing a digital bond in Hong Kong. [S:5a0563de8142, p.1; s.1, p.2] A digital bond is a bond whose ownership is recorded on a shared digital ledger. For a bank that arranges or issues digital bonds, the scheme's conditions affect whether a deal can qualify for a grant.

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Run by | Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) [S:5a0563de8142, p.1] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | In force (initial three-year period) [S:5a0563de8142, p.1] |
| Started | Applications opened 28 Nov 2024. Bonds issued on or after 16 Oct 2024 can apply. [S:633ce27d4f9b, paras 1, 3]; [S:5a0563de8142, p.1 fn 1] |
| Next official date | End of the initial three years from 28 Nov 2024. The sources reviewed show no decision on renewal. [S:633ce27d4f9b, para 3] |
| Covered in | [C5](#m-C5), [E3](#m-E3) |
## What it is

The DBGS refunds half of the eligible costs of issuing a digital bond. [S:5a0563de8142, s.1, p.2] A Half Grant pays up to HK$1.25 million. It applies when the bond meets only the Basic Requirements (the entry conditions). [S:5a0563de8142, s.1, p.2] A Full Grant pays up to HK$2.5 million. It applies when the bond also meets all the Additional Requirements. [S:5a0563de8142, s.1, p.2] Each issuer, counted together with its associates, can get grants for two issues at most. [S:5a0563de8142, s.1, p.2] Associates are, broadly, firms that control the issuer, firms the issuer controls, and firms under the same control as the issuer. [S:5a0563de8142, s.1, p.2] To qualify at all, half or more of the lead arrangers (the firms that organise and sell the issue) must be recognised arrangers. [S:5a0563de8142, s.2, p.3] Recognised arrangers are, in general, arrangers with substantial bond market operations in Hong Kong. [S:5a0563de8142, s.2, p.3] The bond also needs one of two things. [S:5a0563de8142, s.2, p.3] One is a distributed ledger technology (DLT) team with a substantial Hong Kong presence. [S:5a0563de8142, s.2, p.3] The other is issuance on a DLT platform run by the Central Moneymarkets Unit (CMU), the HKMA's bond settlement system. [S:5a0563de8142, s.2, p.3] DLT is a shared digital record kept in step across many computers. The HKMA reserves the absolute right to decide whether a bond meets the requirements and how much to grant. [S:5a0563de8142, p.1] The HKMA may also adjust the scheme. [S:5a0563de8142, p.1]

## Timeline

| Date | Milestone | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16 Oct 2024 | Scheme announced in the Policy Address; bonds issued from this date can apply | Announced | [S:5a0563de8142, p.1 fn 1] |
| 28 Nov 2024 | HKMA launches the DBGS and opens applications | In force | [S:633ce27d4f9b, paras 1, 3] |
| 28 Nov 2024 | Guideline on the DBGS issued | In force | [S:5a0563de8142, p.1] |
| 25 Feb 2026 | Budget says the HKMA will use the DBGS to encourage more digital bond issues | Stated target | [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 97] |
| 16 Jul 2026 | HKMA one-page scheme summary published | Reference | [S:2397140df663, p.1] |
| Nov 2027 | Initial three-year period ends (three years from 28 Nov 2024) | Stated period | [S:633ce27d4f9b, para 3] |

## What it means for your bank

- Arranger roles matter if the bank arranges bonds. Half or more of the lead arrangers must be recognised arrangers for the issue to qualify. [S:5a0563de8142, s.2, p.3]
- The Full Grant needs a DLT platform provider that is not one of the issuer's associates. [S:5a0563de8142, s.3, p.4; s.1 fn 3, p.2] So a bank issuing on its own group's platform would not meet that test. [S:5a0563de8142, s.3, p.4; s.1 fn 3, p.2]
- The Full Grant has three more conditions: [S:5a0563de8142, s.3, p.4]
  - an issue size of at least HK$1 billion; [S:5a0563de8142, s.3, p.4]
  - five or more investors not associated with the issuer or the platform provider; and [S:5a0563de8142, s.3, p.4]
  - a listing on the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong, or on a virtual asset (crypto) trading platform licensed by the Securities and Futures Commission. [S:5a0563de8142, s.3, p.4]
- Two kinds of cost are not eligible expenses: [S:5a0563de8142, s.4 and fn 7, p.5]
  - fees paid to DLT platform providers or arrangers that are associates of the issuer; and [S:5a0563de8142, s.4 and fn 7, p.5]
  - costs covered by other grant schemes. [S:5a0563de8142, s.4 and fn 7, p.5]
- A green digital bond (one that funds environmental projects) can claim general issuance costs under only one scheme. [S:5a0563de8142, s.4, p.5] The choice is the DBGS or Track I of the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme. [S:5a0563de8142, s.4, p.5]
- The issuer, a lead arranger or the DLT platform provider may apply formally within three months after issue. [S:5a0563de8142, s.5, p.6] An optional consultation with the HKMA is available before applying, either before or after issue. [S:5a0563de8142, s.5, p.6]

## Talking points

- **To the CCO:** The grant is a subsidy. The HKMA reserves the absolute right to decide eligibility and the amount. [S:5a0563de8142, p.1]
- **To business heads:** Clients can recover half of eligible expenses, up to HK$2.5 million per issue. Each issuer, with its associates, can do this for two issues at most. [S:5a0563de8142, s.1, p.2]
- **To the CEO:** The 2026-27 Budget says the HKMA will use the scheme to encourage more digital bond issues in Hong Kong. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 97]
- **To Risk:** An issuer that uses a DLT platform provided by its own associate cannot get the Full Grant. The Half Grant is then the most it can get. [S:5a0563de8142, s.3, p.4]

## Key documents

1. Guideline on the Digital Bond Grant Scheme — HKMA — 28 Nov 2024 — read ss.1-5 on amounts, conditions, expenses and timing — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/media/eng/doc/key-functions/ifc/bond-market-development/Guideline_on_the_Digital_Bond_Grant_Scheme.pdf
2. HKMA launches Digital Bond Grant Scheme — HKMA — 28 Nov 2024 — read paras 1-3 — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/news-and-media/press-releases/2024/11/20241128-3/
3. Digital Bond Grant Scheme (summary sheet) — HKMA — Jul 2026 — a one-page checklist of conditions — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/media/eng/doc/key-functions/ifc/bond-market-development/DBGS_Eng.pdf

title: Digital bonds: Genesis, Evergreen and the public-sector issues
md:
Digital bonds (also called tokenised bonds) are bonds whose ownership is recorded as digital tokens on a shared ledger. Hong Kong's work on them began with a 2021 test called Project Genesis. [S:fc3eb72031c6, para 5]; [S:4290ec1111e3, para 7] Since then, the Government has issued three green bonds in digital form, and the Hong Kong Mortgage Corporation (HKMC) issued its own digital bond in 2026. [S:fc3eb72031c6, para 5]; [S:4290ec1111e3, para 7]; [S:6aa27ee8b400, para 1] For banks, the section below on what it means for your bank covers the custody, settlement and licensing points.

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Run by | Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA), acting for the Hong Kong Government on its bonds; HKMC for its own issue [S:a0841967c871, para 5]; [S:6aa27ee8b400, para 1]. Official titles say HKSAR (Hong Kong Special Administrative Region) Government. |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | Issued (latest issue dated 15 Jun 2026). The Policy Address says digital bond issuance will be made regular. [S:6aa27ee8b400, Annex]; [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(i)] |
| Started | 2021 (Project Genesis proof of concept, a small test of whether the idea works) [S:fc3eb72031c6, para 5]; [S:4290ec1111e3, para 7] |
| Next official date | No date given. The Budget says tokenised bonds will keep being issued on a regular basis. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 97] |
| Covered in | [C5](#m-C5), [E2](#m-E2), [A3](#m-A3), [E3](#m-E3) |
## What it is

The HKMA started work on bond tokenisation in 2021. [S:fc3eb72031c6, para 5] That first step was a proof of concept run with the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) Innovation Hub Hong Kong Centre. [S:fc3eb72031c6, para 5] Under Project Evergreen, the HKMA then helped the Government issue tokenised green bonds (bonds that raise money for environmental projects). [S:64cf94cf2036, para 2] The first was a HK$800 million bond in February 2023. [S:a0841967c871, para 1] It was described as the first tokenised green bond issued by any government. [S:a0841967c871, para 1] It settled on a T+1 basis, meaning one business day after the trade date. [S:a0841967c871, paras 3-4] Settlement ran through the Central Moneymarkets Unit (CMU), the HKMA's bond settlement system. [S:a0841967c871, paras 3-4] Settlements in the CMU carry statutory settlement finality: the law treats them as final. [S:a0841967c871, paras 3-4] The HKMA's August 2023 report reviewed Hong Kong statutes. [S:a0b44be27c40, para 28, p.12] It found none that sets the form debt securities (such as bonds) must take when issued. [S:a0b44be27c40, para 28, p.12] A multi-currency issue (one sold in several currencies) of about HK$6 billion followed in February 2024. [S:4290ec1111e3, para 1] In November 2025, a HK$10 billion issue became the first digital bond to offer settlement in tokenised central bank money. [S:ac6cd085a325, paras 1, 8] The two options were e-HKD (a digital form of the Hong Kong dollar) and e-CNY (a digital form of China's renminbi). [S:ac6cd085a325, paras 1, 8] In June 2026, the HKMC priced about HK$12 billion of digital bonds. [S:6aa27ee8b400, paras 1, 4] The bonds were created on a distributed ledger technology (DLT) platform run by the CMU. [S:6aa27ee8b400, paras 1, 4] DLT is a shared digital record kept in step across many computers.

## Timeline

| Date | Milestone | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2021 | Project Genesis proof of concept with the BIS Innovation Hub | Research | [S:fc3eb72031c6, para 5]; [S:4290ec1111e3, para 7] |
| 31 Oct 2022 | Policy Statement names a tokenised green bond pilot | Historical | [S:f587b828e3fa, para 10(b)] |
| 16 Feb 2023 | HK$800m tokenised Government green bond settles | Issued | [S:a0841967c871, para 1; summary terms, 'Settlement'] |
| 24 Aug 2023 | HKMA report "Bond Tokenisation in Hong Kong" released | Research | [S:b7e1bb6b44ae, para 1] |
| 7 Feb 2024 | About HK$6bn multi-currency digital green bonds offered | Issued | [S:4290ec1111e3, para 1] |
| By 28 Nov 2024 | EvergreenHub (HKMA digital bond knowledge library) launched | Launched | [S:64cf94cf2036, para 8] |
| 10 Nov 2025 | HK$10bn digital green bonds priced, with an option to settle in e-HKD or e-CNY | Issued | [S:ac6cd085a325, paras 2, 8] |
| 10 Jun 2026 | HKMC prices about HK$12bn digital bonds (issue date 15 Jun 2026) | Issued | [S:6aa27ee8b400, para 1; Annex] |
| 16 Sep 2026 | Policy Address: digital bond issuance to be made regular | Stated target | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(i)] |

## What it means for your bank

- In Evergreen, only custodians (firms that hold securities for clients) could open token accounts on the platform. [S:a0b44be27c40, para 45, p.16] Each custodian had to be a CMU participant and be onboarded (signed up and approved) to the platform. [S:a0b44be27c40, para 45, p.16] Other investors held the bonds through those custodians. The custodians recorded those investors' interests in their own books. [S:a0b44be27c40, para 45, p.16]
- The report also covers platforms where investors are onboarded themselves. [S:a0b44be27c40, para 44, p.16] There, the report's starting point is for the platform operator to run know-your-customer checks (confirming who each client is). Custodians share this role, as appropriate. [S:a0b44be27c40, para 44, p.16] The same starting point applies to the steps that help clients meet anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing rules. [S:a0b44be27c40, para 44, p.16]
- By law, the CMU is treated as a designated clearing and settlement system (a system the HKMA formally oversees). [S:a0b44be27c40, paras 36-38, pp.14-15] So its settlements have statutory finality. [S:a0b44be27c40, paras 36-38, pp.14-15] Another DLT platform gets that legal finality only if the HKMA designates it. Otherwise, the parties can agree finality in their contracts. [S:a0b44be27c40, paras 36-38, pp.14-15]
- The report says existing securities licensing and offering rules also apply to issuing or distributing digital bonds. [S:a0b44be27c40, para 23, p.11] These rules sit in the Securities and Futures Ordinance (SFO), Hong Kong's main securities law. [S:a0b44be27c40, para 23, p.11]
- The HKMA's February 2024 circular (formal notice to banks) on tokenised products does not cover products regulated under the SFO. [S:b2719f3dcb37, 'Coverage' and fn 2, p.1] Those products follow the relevant requirements of the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) and the HKMA. [S:b2719f3dcb37, 'Coverage' and fn 2, p.1] One example is the SFC's November 2023 circular on tokenised securities. [S:b2719f3dcb37, 'Coverage' and fn 2, p.1]

## Talking points

- **To the CCO:** The Evergreen report says existing SFO licensing and offering rules also apply to digital bonds. [S:a0b44be27c40, para 23, p.11]
- **To business heads:** Sixteen financial institutions arranged the HKMC deal, and settlement fell from T+5 to T+3 (five business days to three). Investors could use existing CMU links to Euroclear and Clearstream, two international settlement systems. [S:6aa27ee8b400, paras 5, 8]
- **To the CEO:** The Policy Address says Hong Kong-issued digital bonds took nearly half the global market from 2025 to mid-2026. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35]
- **To Risk:** The Evergreen report notes that the new capabilities of DLT platforms are largely untested in financial markets. It suggests continuity plans, including for a move to another platform. [S:a0b44be27c40, para 47, p.17]

## Key documents

1. Bond Tokenisation in Hong Kong (Project Evergreen report) — HKMA — 24 Aug 2023 — read paras 23-47 on law, custody and settlement — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/media/eng/doc/key-information/press-release/2023/20230824e3a1.pdf
2. HKSAR Government's Third Digital Green Bonds Offering — HKMA — 11 Nov 2025 — read paras 1-10 and key features — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/news-and-media/press-releases/2025/11/20251111-6/
3. HKMC's HK$12 billion inaugural public digital bond issuance — HKMC (via HKMA) — 11 Jun 2026 — read paras 1-5 and the Annex — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/news-and-media/press-releases/2026/06/20260611-3/
4. EvergreenHub digital bond knowledge repository — HKMA — updated Jul 2026 — use as a reference index — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/key-functions/international-financial-centre/bond-market-development/digital-bond-knowledge-repository/
5. HKSAR Government's Digital Green Bonds Offering — HKMA — 7 Feb 2024 — read footnotes 2-3 on settlement and title — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/news-and-media/press-releases/2024/02/20240207-6/

title: e-HKD (digital Hong Kong dollar)
md:
e-HKD is the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) study of a possible Hong Kong central bank digital currency (CBDC). [S:d51dc8884c8a, opening paragraph] A CBDC is digital money issued by a central bank. It matters to your bank because the work now focuses on wholesale use by financial institutions such as banks. [S:d51dc8884c8a, opening paragraph] The HKMA has not decided whether to launch an e-HKD. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Policy Stance and Three-Rail Approach']

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Run by | HKMA [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'e-HKD for financial institutions' section] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | Research (for retail use by the public, groundwork is done but there is no launch decision); wholesale use between financial institutions is the stated priority [S:6bd9e65817c4, para 4]; [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'e-HKD for individuals and corporates'; 'Policy Stance and Three-Rail Approach'] |
| Started | 2017, with Project LionRock (an early wholesale test) [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'e-HKD for financial institutions' section] |
| Next official date | 2026: real-value e-HKD payments for after-hours derivatives trading with Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing (HKEX) (stated target) [S:ef3648ff1610, para 36(v)] |
| Covered in | [E2](#m-E2), [A3](#m-A3), [E1](#m-E1), [E3](#m-E3) |
## What it is

The HKMA began in 2017 with Project LionRock. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'e-HKD for financial institutions' section] It was a proof of concept (an early test that an idea works) on large-value payments and delivery-versus-payment settlement. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'e-HKD for financial institutions' section] Delivery versus payment means an asset and its payment change hands at the same moment.

The HKMA then consulted on a retail e-HKD, meaning one for the public. It did so through a 2021 technical paper and a 2022 policy paper. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'HKMA's Policy Stance on e-HKD used in retail applications'] The technical paper proposed a two-tier model, in which commercial banks distribute e-HKD. [S:59a20457a2fc, Executive Summary points 3-4] The paper said its design was not a blueprint. [S:59a20457a2fc, Executive Summary points 3-4]

In September 2022 the HKMA set out a three-rail approach (three parallel tracks of work). [S:35cb94c89a11, Rail 1 section, p.10] Its early legal research suggested existing law may not give enough certainty to issue a digital form of legal tender. [S:35cb94c89a11, Rail 1 section, p.10] Legal tender is money that the law recognises for paying debts.

Industry pilots ran in two phases. [S:2f93aa2b9560, paras 1-2] In September 2024 the HKMA renamed the project e-HKD+ so that it also covers tokenised deposits (digital versions of bank deposits). [S:2f93aa2b9560, paras 1-2] In October 2025 the HKMA said the near-term priority is wholesale payments rather than retail use. [S:6bd9e65817c4, para 4] The HKMA has not decided whether, or when, it will introduce an e-HKD. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Policy Stance and Three-Rail Approach']

## Timeline

| Date | Milestone | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2017 | Project LionRock wholesale proof of concept | Research | [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'e-HKD for financial institutions' section] |
| 4 Oct 2021 | Technical paper proposes a two-tier design | Superseded | [S:59a20457a2fc, Executive Summary points 3-5] |
| 27 Apr 2022 | HKMA publishes a policy and design paper | Research | [S:3b42966a786e, Sections 1 and 7] |
| 20 Sep 2022 | HKMA sets out the three-rail approach | Research | [S:35cb94c89a11, Rail 1 section, p.9] |
| 18 May 2023 | Phase 1 pilots start with 16 firms | Research | [S:933b9f10e3b2, para 1] |
| 30 Oct 2023 | Phase 1 report | Research | [S:9f8886b0fb21, Executive Summary, p.6] |
| 23 Sep 2024 | Phase 2 starts; project renamed e-HKD+ | Research | [S:2f93aa2b9560, paras 1-2] |
| 28 Oct 2025 | Phase 2 report; wholesale uses become the priority | Research | [S:6bd9e65817c4, para 4] |
| 11 Nov 2025 | Government digital green bonds offer an option to settle in e-HKD | Issued | [S:ac6cd085a325, 'Integration of digital money' paragraph] |
| H1 2026 | Target to finish groundwork for possible retail use. The HKMA's CBDC web page now says this work is done. | Research | [S:6bd9e65817c4, para 5]; [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'e-HKD for individuals and corporates'] |
| 2026 | Real-value e-HKD payments for after-hours derivatives trading with HKEX | Stated target | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 36(v)] |

## What it means for your bank

- The HKMA has made no policy decision on whether, or when, it would introduce an e-HKD. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Policy Stance and Three-Rail Approach'] The 2021 technical paper says its design is not a blueprint for e-HKD. [S:59a20457a2fc, Executive Summary point 4]
- The April 2022 paper said full anonymity is not a realistic option. [S:3b42966a786e, Section 1, p.4; Section 5.3, p.34] The reason is the requirements against money laundering and terrorist financing. [S:3b42966a786e, Section 1, p.4; Section 5.3, p.34] It noted that tiered wallets are a common answer. [S:3b42966a786e, Section 1, p.4; Section 5.3, p.34] Tiered wallets give users higher limits when they share more identity details.
- The same paper looked at a two-tier model. [S:3b42966a786e, Section 5.4, p.35] It said customer-facing institutions could be given the job of customer due diligence (checking who customers are) and record-keeping. [S:3b42966a786e, Section 5.4, p.35]
- Phase 2 found that the public sees e-HKD and tokenised deposits in a similar light, because people trust banks highly. [S:6bd9e65817c4, para 3]
- The HKMA says it will publish common token standards (shared technical rules for digital tokens) from the e-HKD Industry Forum. [S:6bd9e65817c4, para 6]

## Talking points

- **To the CCO:** No decision exists to introduce an e-HKD. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Policy Stance and Three-Rail Approach'] The 2022 paper saw the firms that distribute e-HKD as the ones that could handle customer due diligence. [S:3b42966a786e, Section 5.4, p.35]
- **To business heads:** The HKMA's e-HKD focus is now wholesale payments, supporting tokenisation and cross-border settlement. [S:6bd9e65817c4, para 4]
- **To the CEO:** The Government's November 2025 digital green bonds offered settlement in e-HKD and e-CNY (the Mainland's digital renminbi). No digital bond offering anywhere had offered this before. [S:ac6cd085a325, 'Integration of digital money' paragraph]
- **To Risk:** In Phase 2, privacy tools called zero-knowledge proofs made transactions up to 320 times costlier in gas fees (network transaction fees). [S:bdefe7fc69d4, Section 4 'Privacy', PDF p.34]

title: Project Ensemble
md:
Project Ensemble is a Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) project on wholesale central bank digital currency. It supports settling tokenised money (money held as digital tokens) between banks. [S:5a9cad53f2be, para 1] It matters to your bank because it is now a live pilot with real-value deals (EnsembleTX). [S:8b67e8dc510f, para 1] The HKMA invites parties with real-value uses for tokenised deposits to take part. [S:8b67e8dc510f, para 5]

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Run by | HKMA, advised on standards by an industry group called the Architecture Community [S:0169bc8fbb4d, paras 1-3] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | Pilot (EnsembleTX is to run throughout 2026) [S:8b67e8dc510f, paras 1, 3] |
| Started | 7 Mar 2024 [S:5a9cad53f2be, para 1] |
| Next official date | Around end-2026: 24/7 operations and settlement in central bank digital currency (CBDC) under EnsembleTX (stated target) [S:ef3648ff1610, para 50] |
| Covered in | [C5](#m-C5), [E1](#m-E1), [E2](#m-E2), [A3](#m-A3), [E3](#m-E3) |
## What it is

Ensemble explores new market infrastructure, meaning the shared systems that banks use to settle deals. [S:5a9cad53f2be, para 2] It tests how banks can settle tokenised money with each other using wholesale CBDC (wCBDC). [S:5a9cad53f2be, para 2; S:460620ab7f2b, footnote 1] Wholesale CBDC is digital central bank money that only financial institutions use. Ensemble's first focus is tokenised deposits. [S:5a9cad53f2be, para 2] These are digital versions of ordinary commercial bank deposits.

The HKMA set up the Architecture Community in May 2024 to develop shared industry standards. [S:0169bc8fbb4d, paras 1-2] A Sandbox (a test environment) followed in August 2024. [S:460620ab7f2b, paras 1-2] Banks in the Architecture Community connected their tokenised-deposit platforms to it. [S:460620ab7f2b, paras 1-2] They were then ready to run two kinds of interbank test. [S:460620ab7f2b, paras 1-2]

- Payment versus payment (PvP): both sides of a currency deal pay at the same moment.
- Delivery versus payment (DvP): an asset and the payment for it change hands at the same moment.

In November 2025 the project moved to EnsembleTX, a pilot that uses real value. [S:8b67e8dc510f, paras 1-2] It starts with trades in tokenised money market funds and with real-time treasury and liquidity uses. [S:8b67e8dc510f, paras 1-2] At first, banks settle with each other through the Hong Kong dollar real-time gross settlement system. [S:8b67e8dc510f, para 3] That system settles each interbank payment in full, one by one, as it happens. The HKMA plans a gradual move to round-the-clock settlement in tokenised central bank money. [S:8b67e8dc510f, para 3]

## Timeline

| Date | Milestone | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 7 Mar 2024 | HKMA unveils Project Ensemble | Superseded (by EnsembleTX) | [S:5a9cad53f2be, para 1] |
| 7 May 2024 | HKMA forms the Ensemble Architecture Community | Pilot (still a partner forum) | [S:0169bc8fbb4d, paras 1, 3]; [S:8b67e8dc510f, para 4] |
| 27 Jun 2024 | HKMA and Banque de France (BDF) announce joint work to link DL3S (the BDF's wholesale CBDC platform) with the Ensemble Sandbox. The work falls under a recent memorandum of understanding (MoU). | Exploratory | [S:0ed273d6f63f, paras 2-3] |
| 28 Aug 2024 | HKMA launches the Ensemble Sandbox, with four test themes | Superseded (by EnsembleTX) | [S:460620ab7f2b, paras 1, 3]; [S:8b67e8dc510f, para 2] |
| 28 Oct 2024 | Tie-ups with Brazil's central bank (Banco Central do Brasil, on its Drex project) and the Bank of Thailand (on Project San) | Exploratory | [S:8d9f12b43ada, para 1]; [S:aabff1db2350, paras 1, 3] |
| 13 Nov 2025 | HKMA launches the EnsembleTX real-value pilot | Pilot | [S:8b67e8dc510f, paras 1-3] |
| 25 Feb 2026 | The Budget says the HKMA will keep upgrading EnsembleTX to support 24/7 settlement | Stated target | [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 109] |
| 2 Mar 2026 | The HKMA, the Shanghai Data Bureau and a national blockchain centre sign an MoU. Electronic bills of lading (digital shipping documents) are to be explored under Ensemble. | Exploratory | [S:eb28508e5032, paras 1-2] |
| Around end-2026 | 24/7 operations and CBDC settlement in EnsembleTX | Stated target | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 50] |
| By end-2026 | Pilot deals done for trade-finance uses of tokenised deposits, studied with the Mainland | Stated target | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 99] |

## What it means for your bank

- The HKMA lists seven Tokenised Deposit Banks. [S:d193f12a5f78, Annex A, p.1] These banks are going to offer tokenised deposits to Hong Kong customers. [S:d193f12a5f78, Annex A, p.1] They will also settle interbank tokenised-deposit deals through EnsembleTX with real value. [S:d193f12a5f78, Annex A, p.1] The HKMA invites others with real-value uses for tokenised deposits to take part. [S:8b67e8dc510f, para 5]
- When customers place tokenised deposits, the HKMA says banks should also meet its circular on tokenised products. [S:b2719f3dcb37, footnote 1, p.1; sections (A)-(C), pp.3-5; 'Implementation', p.6] That circular expects due diligence, disclosure, risk controls and early discussion with the HKMA. [S:b2719f3dcb37, footnote 1, p.1; sections (A)-(C), pp.3-5; 'Implementation', p.6]
- The liquidity coverage ratio (LCR) tests whether a bank holds enough cash-like assets to get through a short period of stress. Under the LCR, a bank may treat qualifying tokenised deposits as deposits or unsecured funding. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3 para 4, pp.89-90] "Qualifying" means a legally binding claim on the bank that can be cashed in at full face value. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3 para 4, pp.89-90] These deposits cannot count as stable retail deposits. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3 para 4, pp.89-90]
- The HKMA has a non-binding note on distributed ledger technology (shared digital record-keeping). It sets out what the HKMA would expect in four areas. [S:1884530ff235, Introduction, 4th bullet; items 2-4 and 8] These are network choice, smart contracts, private-key security, and legal risks such as settlement finality. [S:1884530ff235, Introduction, 4th bullet; items 2-4 and 8] Smart contracts are programs that run by themselves on the ledger. Settlement finality is the point at which a payment becomes final and irreversible.
- Before a full launch, a bank can use the Supervisory Incubator to check its risk controls with a dedicated HKMA team. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, paras 2-3] Tokenised deposits are a core focus of the Incubator. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, paras 2-3]

## Talking points

- **To the CCO:** EnsembleTX is a pilot, not a rulebook. [S:8b67e8dc510f, para 1] Customer tokenised deposits still fall under the HKMA's tokenised-products circular, which expects early discussion with the HKMA. [S:b2719f3dcb37, footnote 1; 'Implementation', p.6]
- **To business heads:** The pilot starts with tokenised money market funds and real-time treasury uses. [S:8b67e8dc510f, paras 2 and 5] The HKMA invites proposals for new real-value uses of tokenised deposits. [S:8b67e8dc510f, paras 2 and 5]
- **To the CEO:** The 2026 Policy Address says the HKMA plans 24/7 operations and CBDC settlement for EnsembleTX by around end-2026. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 50]
- **To Risk:** Tokenised deposits cannot get the LCR treatment for stable retail deposits. If holders cannot always be identified, they count as other unsecured wholesale funding. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3 para 4, p.89]

## Key documents

1. HKMA announces the new phase of Project Ensemble to support real-value transactions in tokenised deposits and digital assets — HKMA — 13 Nov 2025 — read paras 1-5 — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/news-and-media/press-releases/2025/11/20251113-3/
2. Annex A and Annex B to the EnsembleTX release — HKMA — 13 Nov 2025 — read both for participant lists and bank roles — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/media/eng/doc/key-information/press-release/2025/20251113e3a1.pdf
3. HKMA unveils Project Ensemble — HKMA — 7 Mar 2024 — read paras 1-6 for the original aims — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/news-and-media/press-releases/2024/03/20240307-5/
4. HKMA launches Project Ensemble Sandbox — HKMA — 28 Aug 2024 — read paras 1-3 and footnote 1 for test themes — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/news-and-media/press-releases/2024/08/20240828-3/
5. The Chief Executive's 2026 Policy Address — Hong Kong Government — 16 Sep 2026 — read paras 50 and 99 — https://www.policyaddress.gov.hk/2026/public/pdf/policy/policy-full_en.pdf
6. Supervisory Policy Manual LM-1 (V.5), on liquidity risk — HKMA — 19 Dec 2025 — read Annex 3 para 4 on tokenised claims — https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20251217-7-EN/LM-1.pdf

title: Project mBridge
md:
Project mBridge is a shared platform where several central banks each issue their own central bank digital currency (CBDC). [S:947fa49606ab, s.1 Executive summary, p.4] A CBDC is digital money issued by a central bank. It matters to your bank because banks can use the platform to settle cross-border payments and foreign exchange (FX) trades directly. [S:947fa49606ab, s.1 Executive summary, p.4] The Government calls it part of Hong Kong's financial market infrastructure. [S:2ffb8727bb2f, Reply (4)]

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Run by | The mBridge project team. Its members are the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA), the Bank of Thailand (BoT), the Central Bank of the United Arab Emirates (CBUAE), the Digital Currency Institute of the People's Bank of China (PBC), and the Bank for International Settlements Innovation Hub (BISIH) Hong Kong Centre. In June 2024 the Saudi Central Bank was welcomed as the next full participant. [S:db56d97e2206, footnote 1, para 3] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | Pilot (at the minimum viable product stage, meaning a first working version). The Government calls it part of Hong Kong's financial market infrastructure. [S:2ffb8727bb2f, Reply (4)] |
| Started | Q4 2019 as Inthanon-LionRock (a joint study by the HKMA and the BoT); renamed in Feb 2021 [S:6b0fae230518, para 1 and footnote 1] |
| Next official date | None stated. The Government says wider public and private participation will come gradually. [S:2ffb8727bb2f, Reply (4)] |
| Covered in | [E2](#m-E2), [E3](#m-E3) |
## What it is

The project began as Inthanon-LionRock, a study by the HKMA and the BoT on using CBDC for cross-border payments. [S:6b0fae230518, para 1 and footnote 1] In February 2021 the PBC's Digital Currency Institute and the CBUAE joined. [S:6b0fae230518, para 1] The project was then renamed the m-CBDC Bridge. [S:6b0fae230518, para 1]

The platform tests FX deals in which both payments settle at the same moment (payment versus payment). [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Project mBridge' section] It tests these deals in real time, around the clock, across several jurisdictions. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Project mBridge' section]

In the 2022 pilot, 20 banks in four jurisdictions made more than 160 payment and FX trades. [S:947fa49606ab, s.1 Executive summary, p.4] The trades were worth over US$22 million in total. [S:947fa49606ab, s.1 Executive summary, p.4]

The platform reached minimum viable product (MVP) stage in June 2024. [S:db56d97e2206, paras 1-2] Each founding central bank's jurisdiction hosts a validating node, meaning a computer that checks and records platform transactions. [S:db56d97e2206, paras 1-2] In October 2025 the Government told the Legislative Council that participating Hong Kong banks set their own fees for mBridge payments. [S:2ffb8727bb2f, Reply (4)]

## Timeline

| Date | Milestone | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q4 2019 | Inthanon-LionRock starts (HKMA and BoT) | Superseded | [S:6b0fae230518, footnote 1] |
| Jan 2020 | Inthanon-LionRock report | Superseded | [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Project Inthanon-LionRock' section] |
| 23 Feb 2021 | The PBC's Digital Currency Institute and the CBUAE join; project renamed m-CBDC Bridge | Superseded | [S:6b0fae230518, para 1] |
| 28 Sep 2021 | Interim report on faster, cheaper payments | Research | [S:0cfb7eee08a3, paras 1, 3] |
| 15 Aug 2022 | Six-week real-value pilot begins | Pilot | [S:947fa49606ab, s.5.1, p.17] |
| 26 Oct 2022 | Pilot results published | Pilot | [S:2c7f151156dc, paras 1-2] |
| Oct 2023 | mBridge update brochure | Pilot | [S:89b8fcadfaa8, p.1] |
| 5 Jun 2024 | MVP reached; Saudi Central Bank welcomed as next full participant | Pilot | [S:db56d97e2206, paras 1, 3] |
| 8 Oct 2025 | Government says mBridge is part of Hong Kong's financial market infrastructure | Pilot | [S:2ffb8727bb2f, Reply (4)] |

## What it means for your bank

- Each bank runs its own compliance checks off the platform before it sends or confirms a payment. [S:947fa49606ab, s.6.5.2, p.30] These include anti-money laundering (AML), counter-terrorist financing (CTF) and sanctions checks. [S:947fa49606ab, s.6.5.2, p.30]
- Each participating bank must follow the AML, CTF and sanctions laws that apply to it. [S:947fa49606ab, s.7.2(d), p.35] The platform only attaches a pass or fail certificate from the bank's own off-platform check. [S:947fa49606ab, s.7.2(d), p.35]
- Banks keep know-your-customer checks (confirming who customers are), AML and counter-terrorist financing compliance off the platform. [S:89b8fcadfaa8, p.3] Each jurisdiction's own rules apply. [S:89b8fcadfaa8, p.3]
- Foreign banks can hold and use another jurisdiction's CBDC. [S:947fa49606ab, s.7.1.1, p.32; S:89b8fcadfaa8, p.2] Only that jurisdiction's domestic banks can ask its central bank to issue or redeem it. [S:947fa49606ab, s.7.1.1, p.32; S:89b8fcadfaa8, p.2]
- Private firms can propose add-on technology or new uses through a BISIH participation form. [S:db56d97e2206, para 4]

## Talking points

- **To the CCO:** On mBridge, AML and sanctions checks stay with each bank, off the platform. [S:947fa49606ab, s.6.5.2, p.30; s.7.2(d), p.35]
- **To business heads:** Participating Hong Kong banks set their own fees for mBridge payments. [S:2ffb8727bb2f, Reply (4)]
- **To the CEO:** Project mBridge reached MVP in June 2024. [S:db56d97e2206, para 1] The Government calls it part of Hong Kong's financial market infrastructure. [S:2ffb8727bb2f, Reply (4)]
- **To Risk:** The 2022 pilot ran on a single central cloud in Hong Kong. The report says keeping data in one cloud raised privacy concerns. [S:947fa49606ab, s.5.1, p.16; s.7.1.3, p.33]

## Key documents

1. Project mBridge: Connecting economies through CBDC — BISIH, HKMA and partner central banks — Oct 2022 — read sections 6.5.2, 7.1 and 7.2 — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/media/eng/doc/key-information/press-release/2022/20221026e3a1.pdf
2. Project mBridge reaches MVP stage — HKMA — 5 Jun 2024 — read paras 1-4 and footnote 1 — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/news-and-media/press-releases/2024/06/20240605-4/
3. Project mBridge Update: Experimenting with a multi-CBDC platform for cross-border payments — BISIH and partners — Oct 2023 — read pages 2-3 — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/media/eng/doc/key-functions/financial-infrastructure/mBridge_publication.pdf

title: Government policy statements and Policy Address items
md:
These are the Government's own strategy papers on digital assets. They include the 2022 Policy Statement, Policy Statement 2.0 in 2025, and the digital-asset targets in the 2025 and 2026 Policy Addresses. [S:f587b828e3fa, p.6, date line]; [S:a29b51bffc6b, paras 2, 4] A Policy Address is the Chief Executive's yearly speech setting out Government policy. For banks, Policy Statement 2.0 proposed the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) as frontline regulator for banks' digital-asset dealing and custody. [S:a29b51bffc6b, paras 5-6]

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Run by | Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau (FSTB) for the policy statements; Chief Executive for Policy Addresses [S:f587b828e3fa, opening paragraph, p.1]; [S:a29b51bffc6b, para 2]; [S:ef3648ff1610, cover page] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | Stated target (Policy Statement 2.0 and 2026 Policy Address); 2022 statement superseded by Policy Statement 2.0, which builds on it [S:a29b51bffc6b, paras 3-4] |
| Started | 31 Oct 2022 [S:f587b828e3fa, p.6, date line] |
| Next official date | Bill on virtual asset (VA) dealing, custody, advisory and management to be introduced in 2026 (stated target) [S:c6df52e680de, Reply part (3)] |
| Covered in | [A3](#m-A3), [A1](#m-A1), [E1](#m-E1), [E3](#m-E3) |
## What it is

The 2022 Policy Statement adopted a simple principle: the same activity and the same risks get the same regulation. [S:f587b828e3fa, paras 4, 6] It also announced work on a licensing regime for VA service providers. [S:f587b828e3fa, paras 4, 6] It listed three pilots:

- an issue of non-fungible tokens (unique digital tokens) [S:f587b828e3fa, para 10]
- a tokenised Government green bond, meaning a bond recorded as digital tokens [S:f587b828e3fa, para 10]
- e-HKD (a possible digital Hong Kong dollar) [S:f587b828e3fa, para 10]

Policy Statement 2.0 (June 2025) set out the LEAP framework. LEAP stands for four areas of work: [S:a29b51bffc6b, para 4]

- **L**egal and regulatory streamlining
- **E**xpanding tokenised products
- **A**dvancing use cases and cross-sector collaboration
- **P**eople and partnership development

Policy Statement 2.0 proposed the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) as lead authority to license and register digital-asset dealers and custodians. [S:a29b51bffc6b, paras 5-6] It proposed the HKMA as frontline regulator for banks. [S:a29b51bffc6b, paras 5-6] Policy Statement 2.0 also switched the Government's term to *digital assets*. [S:a29b51bffc6b, footnote 1] *Virtual asset* is still the term defined in the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (AMLO). [S:7395a53cc85a, Note] The 2026 Policy Address adds targets for the HKMA and SFC, some with dates. [S:ef3648ff1610, paras 35, 49-50]

## Timeline

| Date | Milestone | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 31 Oct 2022 | Policy Statement on Development of VA in Hong Kong | Superseded | [S:f587b828e3fa, p.6, date line]; [S:a29b51bffc6b, para 3] |
| 26 Jun 2025 | Policy Statement 2.0 (LEAP) | Stated target | [S:a29b51bffc6b, paras 4-6] |

A digital asset platform this year from CMU OmniClear, the company that runs the Central Moneymarkets Unit (CMU) for the HKMA | Stated target | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii), (iv)] |

## What it means for your bank

- Policy Statement 2.0 said the HKMA would be the frontline regulator for banks. The HKMA was to supervise banks' digital-asset dealing and custody. [S:a29b51bffc6b, paras 5-6] Policy Statement 2.0 proposed the SFC as the lead authority for licensing and registration. [S:a29b51bffc6b, paras 5-6]
- The 2025 Policy Address said the HKMA would encourage banks to introduce tokenised deposits. These are bank deposits recorded as digital tokens. [S:cc2fa9fc0772, para 103, p.40] The HKMA would also promote live deals in tokenised assets, such as settling tokenised money market funds with tokenised deposits. [S:cc2fa9fc0772, para 103, p.40]
- The same paragraph said the HKMA would encourage banks to use the supervisory sandbox to improve their risk management. The sandbox lets banks test new technology with HKMA oversight. [S:cc2fa9fc0772, para 103, p.40]
- Separately, the HKMA expects the board of each authorized institution to oversee a strategic business plan on technology change. Authorized institutions are the banks and deposit-takers the HKMA authorizes. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, para 4, pp.1-2] The board should sign off the plan within six months of the HKMA's 9 March 2026 circular. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, para 4, pp.1-2]

## Talking points

- **To the CCO:** The Government now says *digital assets*. But *virtual asset* is still the defined term in AMLO. [S:a29b51bffc6b, footnote 1]; [S:7395a53cc85a, Note]

- **To the CEO:** The Government's stated 2026 target is one bill for VA dealing, custody, advisory and management licensing. [S:c6df52e680de, Reply part (3)]
- **To Risk:** Customs plans a system to analyse digital-asset transactions by 2029. The system is part of the Customs anti-money laundering big-data platform. [S:ef3648ff1610, Annex (I) New Indicators, item 209]

title: Relevant Stablecoins: dealing, advice and trading
md:
Relevant Stablecoins are stablecoins issued under a Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) licence. [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1] A stablecoin is a digital token meant to keep a steady value, usually against an official currency. In May 2026, the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) eased how their virtual-asset (VA) conduct rules apply to these coins. [S:a0bd48559762, p.1; S:19d52ade6849, p.1] This page also covers the stated plan for trading them on licensed platforms. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 49(iii)] Why it matters to your bank: some VA rules are lighter for these coins. For example, dealing only in these coins needs no Type 1 registration (the SFC registration for dealing in securities). [S:a0bd48559762, para (2), p.3]

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Run by | Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) for banks; Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) for trading platforms and licensed corporations [S:a0bd48559762, opening paragraph, p.1]; [S:19d52ade6849, opening paragraph, p.1] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | In force (since 27 May 2026) [S:a0bd48559762, p.1]; [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1] |
| Started | 27 May 2026 [S:a0bd48559762, p.1]; [S:19d52ade6849, p.1] |
| Next official date | None fixed. The Chief Executive's Policy Address says the SFC will promote stablecoin trading on licensed platforms (stated target) [S:ef3648ff1610, para 49(iii)] |
| Covered in | [C1](#m-C1), [C4](#m-C4), [B2](#m-B2), [C7](#m-C7), [E1](#m-E1) |
## What it is

A Relevant Stablecoin is a specified stablecoin (a class defined in the law) issued under a licence granted under the Stablecoins Ordinance. [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1]

After the Ordinance came into force, the HKMA and the SFC reviewed how their joint circulars on VA activities should apply to these coins. [S:a0bd48559762, Background, pp.1-2] They took into account that the coins are pegged to a currency. [S:a0bd48559762, Background, pp.1-2]

The HKMA's circular to registered institutions (RIs) sets out the changes. RIs are banks that the SFC has registered for securities business. [S:a0bd48559762, 'Detailed guidance', p.2] Updated terms and conditions are in Appendices A1 and A2. [S:a0bd48559762, 'Detailed guidance', p.2]

A separate HKMA letter points all authorized institutions (AIs) to the same standards. AIs are the banks and deposit-taking companies the HKMA authorizes. [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1]

The SFC's circular 26EC26 covers virtual asset trading platforms (VATPs) and licensed corporations (LCs), meaning firms licensed by the SFC. [S:19d52ade6849, opening paragraph and fn 2, p.1] It refers RIs to the HKMA circular. [S:19d52ade6849, opening paragraph and fn 2, p.1]

The HKMA letter says its guidance should not be read as treating these coins as investment products. [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1]

## Timeline

| Date | Milestone | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Aug 2025 | Stablecoins Ordinance comes into force | In force | [S:0df2de5234dc, para 1] |
| 10 Apr 2026 | First two issuer licences take effect | In force | [S:270f1f7324ab, Register table] |
| 27 May 2026 | HKMA circular to RIs, with Appendices A1/A2 | In force | [S:a0bd48559762, p.1] |
| 27 May 2026 | HKMA letter to all AIs | In force | [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1] |
| 27 May 2026 | SFC circular 26EC26 to VATPs and LCs | In force | [S:19d52ade6849, p.1, opening paragraph] |
| 16 Sep 2026 | Policy Address: SFC to promote stablecoin trading on licensed platforms, and their use to settle tokenised money market funds (cash-like funds in token form) | Stated target | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 49(iii)] |

## What it means for your bank

- RIs may now deal in a Relevant Stablecoin through the licensed issuer, not only through a VA trading platform. [S:a0bd48559762, para (1), p.3]
- Dealing only in Relevant Stablecoins needs no Type 1 registration. [S:a0bd48559762, para (2), p.3] The conduct terms in Appendix A1 still apply. [S:a0bd48559762, para (2), p.3]
- No VA knowledge test (a check that the client understands VA) is needed for accounts clearly ring-fenced (kept separate) for Relevant Stablecoins only. [S:a0bd48559762, para (3)(a) and fn 4, p.4] If the account adds any other VA, the full rules apply again. [S:a0bd48559762, para (3)(a) and fn 4, p.4]
- When dealing or advising, the bank should disclose material information on how each coin keeps its value stable. It should also disclose how redemption (cashing in) of the coin works. [S:a0bd48559762, para (5), p.5; para (10), p.7]
- Advice should rest on thorough analysis, such as what the client wants to use the coin for. [S:a0bd48559762, para (8), p.6] Commission rebates or other benefits should not be the main reason to recommend a coin. [S:a0bd48559762, para (8), p.6]
- The HKMA reminds RIs to give it and the SFC advance notice before they start these activities or change them materially. [S:a0bd48559762, Implementation, p.9] The HKMA reminds all AIs to discuss these activities with it in advance. [S:1babdb609fc8, 'Implementation', p.2]
- The changes do not apply to other stablecoins. [S:a0bd48559762, 'Detailed guidance' and footnote 3, p.2] The joint-circular rules and the HKMA circular to RIs also do not apply to:
  - AIs that are not RIs;
  - a licensed issuer, for its own coin. [S:a0bd48559762, 'Detailed guidance' and footnote 3, p.2]
- The HKMA expects both of these groups to meet similar standards that it issues separately. [S:a0bd48559762, 'Detailed guidance' and footnote 3, p.2]

## Talking points

- **To the CCO:** As a registered institution, we follow the HKMA circular to RIs. Circular 26EC26 sets standards for VATPs and LCs. [S:19d52ade6849, opening paragraph and fn 2, p.1] RIs are still reminded to notify both regulators in advance. [S:a0bd48559762, Implementation, p.9]
- **To business heads:** Clients with Relevant-Stablecoin-only accounts need no VA knowledge test. They also need no VA exposure limit (cap on a client's VA holdings). Offering those clients any other VA brings back the full rules. [S:a0bd48559762, para (3)(a)-(b) and fn 4, pp.4-5]
- **To the CEO:** The Policy Address says the SFC will promote trading of regulated stablecoins on licensed platforms. That includes their use to settle tokenised money market funds. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 49(iii)]
- **To Risk:** Only coins issued under an HKMA licence qualify. [S:19d52ade6849, para 2] The HKMA register lists the licensees. [S:afb6cd0da6ff, para 4]

## Key documents

1. Virtual asset-related activities in relation to relevant stablecoins (circular to RIs) — HKMA — 27 May 2026 — read all nine pages, especially paras (1)-(9) and Implementation — https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20260527-2-EN/20260527-2-EN.pdf
2. Relevant Stablecoin-related Activities (letter to AIs) — HKMA — 27 May 2026 — read both pages — https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20260527-4-EN/20260527-4-EN.pdf
3. Circular on provision of Relevant Stablecoin service by VATPs and LCs (26EC26) — SFC — 27 May 2026 — read paras 2-12 for counterparty rules — https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/api/circular/openFile?lang=EN&refNo=26EC26
4. The Chief Executive's 2026 Policy Address — Hong Kong Government — 16 Sep 2026 — read para 49 — https://www.policyaddress.gov.hk/2026/public/pdf/policy/policy-full_en.pdf
