title: Stablecoin issuer regime (Stablecoins Ordinance, Cap. 656)
md:
The Stablecoins Ordinance (Cap. 656, its chapter number in Hong Kong's laws) is Hong Kong's licensing law for firms that issue fiat-referenced stablecoins. These are digital tokens meant to keep a steady value against an official currency, such as the Hong Kong dollar. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) grants the licences. [S:ad1082eb2ea9, para 2] This page traces the regime from the 2024 sandbox (a supervised test run) to the first licences. It also covers the public register, the review tribunal and complaint handling. Why it matters to your bank: authorized institutions (AIs) may offer licensed coins to customers. [S:7b6c8dc63140, reply (1), para 1] AI is the legal term for banks and deposit-taking companies authorized by the HKMA. An AI can also apply to issue its own coins. [S:fe4baea8dd7d, paras 3.2.1-3.2.3; fns 1, 8]

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Run by | HKMA, which grants licences [S:ad1082eb2ea9, para 2]. A Stablecoin Review Tribunal reviews specified (listed) HKMA decisions. The Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau (FSTB) hosts its web page. [S:16699fe49364, para 1] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | In force (since 1 Aug 2025) [S:0df2de5234dc, para 1] |
| Started | HKMA discussion paper, 12 Jan 2022 [S:2b888e600616, cover page and Section 6] |
| Next official date | None fixed. Licensed coins were expected to launch between mid-2026 and the second half of 2026. That timing was based on the issuers' business plans. [S:c6df52e680de, Reply, first paragraph] |
| Covered in | [C4](#m-C4), [B2](#m-B2), [C3](#m-C3), [D1](#m-D1), [D3](#m-D3), [E3](#m-E3) |
## What it is

The Ordinance requires any business that issues a fiat-referenced stablecoin (FRS) in Hong Kong to hold an HKMA licence. [S:ad1082eb2ea9, para 2] The same applies to an FRS linked to the Hong Kong dollar, wherever it is issued. [S:ad1082eb2ea9, para 2]

A licensee must keep a separate reserve pool (the assets that back the coins) for each type of coin. [S:240be6833157, paras 2.2.1, 2.5.1] Each pool's market value must always be at least the par value (face value) of the coins in circulation. [S:240be6833157, paras 2.2.1, 2.5.1]

Holders must have a right to redeem (cash in) their coins at par. [S:240be6833157, paras 3.3.1, 3.3.3] The issuer should process valid requests within one business day, unless the HKMA approves otherwise. [S:240be6833157, paras 3.3.1, 3.3.3]

Only permitted offerors may offer these coins. An AI is one of them. [S:fe4baea8dd7d, para 2.10.1]

The HKMA licensed the first two issuers with effect from 10 April 2026. [S:afb6cd0da6ff, para 1] It says that if it grants more licences, the total will stay very limited. [S:193316443831, 'Follow-up work', para 3]

## Timeline

| Date | Milestone | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 12 Jan 2022 | HKMA discussion paper on crypto-assets and stablecoins | Superseded | [S:2b888e600616, cover page and Section 6] |
| 27 Dec 2023 | FSTB and HKMA consult on the issuer regime (comments due by 29 Feb 2024) | Superseded | [S:167649d1bc28, cover page and para 3] |
| 12 Mar 2024 | HKMA opens a sandbox for would-be stablecoin issuers | Superseded | [S:f2a668eb3b93, para 1] |
| 17 Jul 2024 | FSTB and HKMA publish consultation conclusions | Superseded | [S:54aa01e7396e, cover page and para 12.1] |
| 18 Jul 2024 | HKMA names the first sandbox participants (three entries; one is a group of three firms) | Superseded | [S:cf1df12c1b58, para 1] |
| 6 Dec 2024 | Stablecoins Bill published in the Government Gazette | Superseded | [S:a9a82f2b38ce, para 1] |
| 21 May 2025 | Legislative Council (LegCo) passes the Bill | Superseded | [S:35e1ac2b815a, para 1] |
| 1 Aug 2025 | Ordinance and HKMA guidelines come into force | In force | [S:0df2de5234dc, para 1]; [S:6c3f349e4f90, para 1] |
| 1 Nov 2025 | Current term of Stablecoin Review Tribunal members starts (runs to 31 Oct 2028) | In force | [S:16699fe49364, para 2] |
| 10 Apr 2026 | First two issuer licences take effect. HKMA points the public to its register | In force | [S:270f1f7324ab, Register table]; [S:afb6cd0da6ff, paras 1, 4] |
| Mid-to-late 2026 | Launch of licensed coins expected | Stated target | [S:c6df52e680de, Reply, first paragraph] |

## What it means for your bank

- As a permitted offeror, the bank may offer coins from licensed issuers to retail and professional investors. [S:7b6c8dc63140, reply (1), para 1] Other specified stablecoins (a class defined in the law) may go to professional investors only. [S:7b6c8dc63140, reply (1), para 1]
- An AI can apply to issue coins. [S:fe4baea8dd7d, paras 3.2.1-3.2.3; fns 1, 8] An AI incorporated overseas needs no local subsidiary. [S:fe4baea8dd7d, paras 3.2.1-3.2.3; fns 1, 8] Some minimum criteria, such as financial resources, do not apply to AI applicants. [S:fe4baea8dd7d, paras 3.2.1-3.2.3; fns 1, 8]
- The HKMA keeps a public register of licensees. It tells the public to use the register to check claims about licensees. [S:afb6cd0da6ff, paras 4-5]
- A place in the sandbox did not mean the HKMA endorsed the firm. Sandbox firms had to apply separately for a licence. [S:f2a668eb3b93, Annex, Objectives, p.1]
- For its own holdings, the bank must notify the HKMA when it acquires a new type of cryptoasset. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2] The bank must treat the asset as Group 2b (the crypto group with the strictest bank capital treatment) until the HKMA agrees its classification. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2]
- The HKMA may assess complaints about an issuer that the issuer has not handled properly. [S:d3e75db3ddb3, 'Lodging Complaint with the HKMA' section] The HKMA generally does not order an issuer to pay compensation. [S:d3e75db3ddb3, 'Lodging Complaint with the HKMA' section]

## Talking points

- **To the CCO:** Only coins from licensed issuers may be offered to retail investors. AIs are permitted offerors. [S:7b6c8dc63140, reply (1), para 1] The HKMA register lists who is licensed. [S:afb6cd0da6ff, paras 4-5]
- **To business heads:** Two issuers hold licences that took effect on 10 April 2026. [S:270f1f7324ab, Register table] The HKMA says any further licences will stay very limited in number. [S:193316443831, 'Follow-up work', para 3]
- **To the CEO:** An AI may apply to issue coins. The financial-resources and business-activities criteria do not apply to it. [S:fe4baea8dd7d, para 3.2.1; fns 1, 8]
- **To Risk:** A licensee must give holders a right to redeem at par. It should process valid requests within one business day. Reserves should be held under trust arrangements with qualified custodians (firms that safekeep assets). [S:240be6833157, paras 2.5.2, 2.5.4, 3.3.1, 3.3.3]

## Key documents

2. Guideline on Supervision of Licensed Stablecoin Issuers — HKMA — 1 Aug 2025 — read sections 2-3 on reserves and redemption — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/media/eng/doc/key-functions/ifc/stablecoin-issuers/Guideline_on_supervision_of_licensed_stablecoin_issuers_eng.pdf
3. Register of Licensees under the Stablecoins Ordinance — HKMA — revised 23 Apr 2026 — lists current licensees — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/regulatory-resources/registers/register-of-licensed-stablecoin-issuers/

5. Stablecoin Review Tribunal — FSTB — undated page — read paras 1-3 on reviews — https://www.fstb.gov.hk/fsb/en/topical/srt.html

title: Supervisory Incubator for DLT
md:
The Supervisory Incubator for distributed ledger technology (DLT) is a Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) scheme for banks. DLT is a shared digital record kept in step across many computers, such as a blockchain. A bank can use the Incubator to check the risk controls for a DLT project with a dedicated HKMA team before full launch. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, para 3] Why banks care: the HKMA says six banks have launched tokenised deposit services through the Incubator. [S:418769c01edc, 'Supervisory Incubator for DLT – where traditional finance and tokenisation meets' section] Tokenised deposits are bank deposits recorded as digital tokens.

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Run by | Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) [S:1b1a0de5de5a, para 1] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | Pilot: Authorized Institutions (AIs: banks and deposit-takers authorized by the HKMA) may apply to join. [S:fae36c380174, p.1; p.2] The HKMA was still promoting the Incubator in March 2026. [S:38e1f67c38df, para 3] |
| Started | 8 Jan 2025 [S:fae36c380174, p.1] |
| Next official date | None stated |
| Covered in | [B2](#m-B2), [B3](#m-B3), [C5](#m-C5), [E2](#m-E2), [E3](#m-E3) |
## What it is

The Incubator is a supervisory arrangement. It helps banks manage the risks of adopting DLT. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, para 2] It pays close attention to risks in services that span DLT and older, existing systems. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, para 2] Tokenised deposits were a core focus from the start. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, para 2]

For each bank, the Incubator offers a single contact point at the HKMA. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, para 3] Through it, the bank can reconfirm that its risk controls are adequate before launch. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, para 3] The bank works with a dedicated HKMA team and can choose to run live trials. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, para 3] Trials take a hands-on, step-by-step approach. [S:fae36c380174, p.1]

For the industry as a whole, the Incubator is to share good practice through guidance, sharing sessions and research. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, para 4] In an HKMA inSight article on 24 October 2025, the HKMA said six banks had launched tokenised deposit services through the Incubator. [S:418769c01edc, 'Supervisory Incubator for DLT – where traditional finance and tokenisation meets' section]

## Timeline

| Date | Milestone | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16 Apr 2024 | HKMA issues non-binding DLT risk-management considerations | In force | [S:1884530ff235, Annex, Introduction] |
| 8 Jan 2025 | Incubator launched at FiNETech4 (an HKMA fintech event); circular (formal HKMA letter) sent to AIs | Pilot | [S:1b1a0de5de5a, paras 1, 6]; [S:fae36c380174, p.1] |
| 24 Oct 2025 | HKMA reports six banks' tokenised deposit services launched through the Incubator | Pilot | [S:418769c01edc, 'Supervisory Incubator for DLT – where traditional finance and tokenisation meets' section] |
| 9 Mar 2026 | Business-model circular says banks' plans may include small real-world trials through the Incubator | In force | [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, para 4] |
| 9 Mar 2026 | HKMA event on Project Ensemble and the Incubator for around 60 banks | Pilot | [S:38e1f67c38df, para 3 and closing note] |

## What it means for your bank

- Joining is voluntary. AIs that want to use the Incubator contact the HKMA. [S:fae36c380174, p.2] The purpose is to reconfirm risk controls before a full launch. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, para 3]
- The HKMA is prepared to give AIs in the Incubator some supervisory flexibility (room in how rules apply). The HKMA decides this case by case. [S:fae36c380174, p.1 and footnote 2] One factor is whether the bank can meet operating principles similar to those for Fintech Supervisory Sandbox trials. The Sandbox is an existing HKMA scheme for limited fintech pilots. [S:fae36c380174, p.1 and footnote 2]
- That flexibility depends on the bank managing trial risks in line with the trial's scale, scope and nature. [S:fae36c380174, p.1]
- Some existing rules might not fit DLT well. Where that mismatch is unintended, the HKMA says it will consider whether rules need adapting or some flexibility is needed. [S:fae36c380174, p.2] The HKMA will do the same where the mismatch goes against the principle of "same activity, same risk, same regulation". [S:fae36c380174, p.2]
- The HKMA's non-binding DLT considerations remain a reference. [S:1884530ff235, Annex, Introduction; items 1-4, 8] They cover:
  - board responsibility;
  - network choice;
  - smart contracts (code on the ledger that runs by itself);
  - legal risks such as settlement finality (the point when a transfer is legally final);
  - private key security (protecting the secret codes that control digital assets).
- The HKMA expects AIs planning new digital-asset activities to discuss them with the HKMA before launch. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, para 5]

## Talking points

- **To the CCO:** The HKMA decides any supervisory flexibility in the Incubator case by case. It depends on how the bank manages trial risks. [S:fae36c380174, p.1 and footnote 2]
- **To business heads:** The HKMA says six banks have launched tokenised deposit services through the Incubator. [S:418769c01edc, 'Supervisory Incubator for DLT – where traditional finance and tokenisation meets' section]
- **To the CEO:** The HKMA's business-model circular says a bank's strategic plan may factor in small real-world trials through the Incubator. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, para 4]
- **To Risk:** The HKMA's DLT considerations say the board and senior management carry full responsibility for DLT adoption and its risks. [S:1884530ff235, Annex item 1]

2. HKMA launches Supervisory Incubator to foster responsible adoption of DLT — HKMA — 8 Jan 2025 — read paras 2-4 — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/news-and-media/press-releases/2025/01/20250108-3/

title: Tokenised Bond Expert Group and the DLT fixed-income law review
md:
Distributed ledger technology (DLT) is a shared digital record kept in step across many computers. The Tokenised Bond Expert Group (TBEG) is a Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) panel of industry experts on tokenised bonds. [S:fc3eb72031c6, paras 1, 3] Tokenised bonds are bonds whose ownership is recorded as digital tokens on DLT. The group works alongside a joint review by the Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau (FSTB) and the HKMA. [S:fc3eb72031c6, paras 1, 3] The review asks whether Hong Kong's laws and rules support using DLT in the bond market. [S:279f10054c6e, para 1] For a bank that issues, arranges or holds tokenised bonds, the review shows where current law already fits. It also shows which legal questions are still open. Fixed income, in the title, means bonds and similar debt.

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Run by | HKMA for the TBEG; FSTB and HKMA jointly for the review [S:fc3eb72031c6, para 1]; [S:279f10054c6e, para 1] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | Exploratory (TBEG); review phase 1 conclusions published 29 Jun 2026 [S:fc3eb72031c6, paras 1-3]; [S:279f10054c6e, para 1] |
| Started | The 2025-26 Budget first announced the review. The TBEG held its first discussions in May 2026 and was announced on 5 Jun 2026. [S:279f10054c6e, para 15]; [S:fc3eb72031c6, paras 1, 3] |
| Next official date | Phase 2 legal review in H2 2026, the second half of the year (stated target) [S:279f10054c6e, para 8]; [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(iii)] |
| Covered in | [C5](#m-C5), [A3](#m-A3), [E1](#m-E1), [E3](#m-E3) |
## What it is

Policy Statement 2.0 said the FSTB and HKMA would lead a review of law and regulation on tokenisation, with bonds as the first focus. [S:a29b51bffc6b, para 9] Tokenisation means representing an asset, such as a bond, as a digital token. The 2026-27 Budget said the Government would issue guidance on registers of debenture holders (official lists of who holds a company's bonds). [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 107] The guidance is to confirm that these registers may be kept on a distributed ledger. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 107] The Budget further said the Government would explore e-signatures for bond documents. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 107] It also named digitised bearer bonds (bonds owned by whoever holds the certificate) as a topic to explore. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 107] The HKMA announced the TBEG on 5 June 2026. [S:fc3eb72031c6, paras 1-2] Its members come from: [S:fc3eb72031c6, paras 1-2]

- industry bodies;
- financial institutions;
- law firms; and
- infrastructure and technology providers.

The group's discussions in May 2026 gave input to the joint review. [S:fc3eb72031c6, para 3] Phase 1 of the review found that current law and regulation are already flexible enough for tokenised bond issues. [S:279f10054c6e, para 1] On 29 June 2026, when the phase 1 findings came out, the Companies Registry published answers to frequently asked questions (FAQs). [S:279f10054c6e, para 6] The FAQs confirm that a register of debenture holders kept on DLT can meet the record-keeping rules in the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622). [S:279f10054c6e, para 6]

## Timeline

| Date | Milestone | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 26 Jun 2025 | Policy Statement 2.0 commits to a tokenisation law review, starting with bonds | Stated target | [S:a29b51bffc6b, para 9] |
| 25 Feb 2026 | Budget sets review topics: DLT registers, e-signatures, bearer bonds | Stated target | [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 107]; [S:279f10054c6e, para 15] |
| May 2026 | First TBEG discussion sessions | Exploratory | [S:fc3eb72031c6, para 3] |
| 5 Jun 2026 | HKMA announces the TBEG | Exploratory | [S:fc3eb72031c6, para 1] |
| 29 Jun 2026 | Phase 1 findings and Companies Registry FAQs | Conclusions published | [S:279f10054c6e, paras 1, 6] |
| H2 2026 | Phase 2 law review (signing documents electronically; possession and transfer of tokens) | Stated target | [S:279f10054c6e, paras 8-11] |
| 16 Sep 2026 | Policy Address: TBEG to launch the phase 2 review with the FSTB | Stated target | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(iii)] |

## What it means for your bank

- Phase 1 created no new obligation. It found the current legal and regulatory setting already flexible enough for tokenised bond issues. [S:279f10054c6e, paras 1, 3]
- The Companies Registry FAQs are the reference point for DLT registers of debenture holders. [S:279f10054c6e, para 6] They matter if the bank keeps or relies on such a register for a Hong Kong company. [S:279f10054c6e, para 6]
- Phase 2 will look at letting issuers sign tokenised bond issue documents electronically. One example is using electronic signatures to create trusts for tokenised bond and fund issues. [S:279f10054c6e, paras 9-11] It will also look at how possession and transfer work for tokenised fixed-income instruments. [S:279f10054c6e, paras 9-11]
- The HKMA says it will review and update the group's membership when needed. [S:fc3eb72031c6, para 4]

## Talking points

- **To the CCO:** Phase 1 changed no law. It confirmed the current rules are flexible enough and added Companies Registry FAQs on DLT registers. [S:279f10054c6e, paras 1, 6]
- **To business heads:** Phase 2 will explore signing tokenised bond issue documents electronically. The goal is a more efficient and automated issuance process. [S:279f10054c6e, para 10]
- **To the CEO:** The HKMA set up the TBEG to explore policy measures, market practices and innovations with industry. [S:fc3eb72031c6, paras 1-2]
- **To Risk:** Possession and transfer of tokenised instruments are topics for the phase 2 review. That review is set for H2 2026. [S:279f10054c6e, paras 8, 11]

## Key documents

1. FSTB and HKMA to further unlock potential of DLT in Hong Kong's fixed income market — FSTB and HKMA — 29 Jun 2026 — read the whole release, especially 'Next phase' — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/news-and-media/press-releases/2026/06/20260629-4/
2. HKMA establishes Tokenised Bond Expert Group — HKMA — 5 Jun 2026 — read paras 1-4 and the Annex of members — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/news-and-media/press-releases/2026/06/20260605-3/
3. 2026-27 Budget — Financial Secretary — 25 Feb 2026 — read para 107 — https://www.budget.gov.hk/2026/eng/pdf/e_budget_speech_2026-27.pdf
4. Policy Statement 2.0 on the Development of Digital Assets in Hong Kong — FSTB — 26 Jun 2025 — read para 9 — https://gia.info.gov.hk/general/202506/26/P2025062600269_500089_1_1750909574183.pdf

title: New VA licensing regimes: dealing, custody, advisory and management
md:
VA stands for virtual asset, such as a crypto token. Hong Kong has four planned licensing regimes for firms that provide dealing, custody, advisory or management services in virtual assets (VAs). One bill under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615) is to bring in all four. [S:c6df52e680de, Reply part (3)]; [S:4a0342268bf2, para 3] This matters to banks because a bank offering VA dealing or custody would register with the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC). The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) is set to supervise the bank day to day. [S:7395a53cc85a, para 4]

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Run by | Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau (FSTB) and Securities and Futures Commission (SFC); Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) as frontline regulator for banks [S:7395a53cc85a, paras 1, 4] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | Conclusions published (all four regimes) [S:ff3df4326e0f, para 1]; [S:4a0342268bf2, para 1] |
| Started | Proposal to license VA over-the-counter (OTC) trading, 8 Feb 2024; revised in the 27 Jun 2025 consultations [S:efcdb0ae3849, para 2.6]; [S:7395a53cc85a, paras 1, 3] |
| Next official date | One bill to the Legislative Council (LegCo) in 2026 (stated target); start dates not set [S:c6df52e680de, Reply part (3)]; [S:6186c01c6649, para 32]; [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 64] |
| Covered in | [E1](#m-E1), [C1](#m-C1), [C3](#m-C3), [A3](#m-A3), [B2](#m-B2) |
## What it is

Today the SFC adds VA terms and conditions to the licences and registrations of firms it already oversees. The dealing, advisory and management regimes will replace that practice. [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 62] The current HKMA–SFC joint circular (a letter both regulators issued together) sets the requirements. Those requirements will become the starting point for these three regimes. [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 62]

The four regimes cover different services:

- **VA dealing** will line up with Type 1 (dealing in securities). [S:6186c01c6649, paras 3, 26] The SFC will require dealers to keep client VAs with VA custodians the SFC regulates. [S:6186c01c6649, paras 3, 26]
- **VA custody** means safekeeping VAs for others. The custodian licence will cover firms that keep private keys for others. Private keys are the secret codes that let someone move a VA. [S:f41a543388bc, paras 6-7, 12] The licence will also cover firms that keep other tools that let someone transfer VAs for others. [S:f41a543388bc, paras 6-7, 12] Custody of tokenised securities alone falls outside the licence. Tokenised securities are securities recorded as digital tokens. [S:f41a543388bc, paras 6-7, 12]
- **VA advisory** will line up with Type 4 (advising on securities). **VA management** will line up with Type 9 (asset management). [S:4a0342268bf2, para 2]; [S:6186c01c6649, fns 9-10]
- **Banks only:** the further consultation said only banks could register with the SFC for advisory and management, rather than be licensed. [S:4a0342268bf2, para 2]; [S:6186c01c6649, fns 9-10]

An earlier proposal had the Commissioner of Customs and Excise license VA OTC spot trading. OTC means deals agreed directly between two parties, not on an exchange. The SFC dealing proposal replaced that approach. [S:efcdb0ae3849, para 2.6]; [S:27d27650e820, paras 1.1, 1.9-1.10]

## Timeline

| Date | Milestone | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8 Feb 2024 | Consultation on licensing VA OTC trading (Customs to run it; banks exempt) | Superseded | [S:efcdb0ae3849, paras 2.6, 2.23] |
| 19 Feb 2025 | ASPIRe (the SFC's VA roadmap) lists OTC and custody licensing | Stated target | [S:d461c2db6af2, Pillar A, Initiative 1] |
| 27 Jun 2025 | Dealing and custodian consultations (to 29 Aug 2025) | Superseded | [S:7395a53cc85a, para 1] |
| 24 Dec 2025 | Dealing and custodian conclusions; advisory and management consultation | Conclusions published | [S:ff3df4326e0f, paras 1, 5] |
| 23 Jan 2026 | Advisory and management consultation closes | Superseded | [S:6186c01c6649, 'Further public consultation', p.3; para 72] |
| 26 May 2026 | Advisory and management conclusions | Conclusions published | [S:4a0342268bf2, para 1] |
| 24 Jun 2026 | Government: one bill for all four regimes this year | Stated target | [S:c6df52e680de, Reply part (3)] |
| 16 Sep 2026 | Policy Address: SFC to improve VA licensing regimes | Stated target | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 49(i)] |

## What it means for your bank

- For VA dealing and custody, a bank would register with the SFC. The HKMA is set to be its frontline regulator, meaning the HKMA supervises the bank day to day. [S:7395a53cc85a, para 4]
- None of the four regimes is planned to let existing firms carry on while they apply. [S:6186c01c6649, paras 31, 35-36]; [S:f41a543388bc, paras 48, 51]; [S:01c5c5c4045f, paras 63, 67]
- Firms the SFC or HKMA already oversee for these services will get a faster approval process. That group includes registered institutions, which are banks registered with the SFC. [S:6186c01c6649, paras 31, 35-36]; [S:f41a543388bc, paras 48, 51]; [S:01c5c5c4045f, paras 63, 67]
- Banks are exempt from the custodians' rule on minimum financial resources. The reason is that HKMA capital requirements already apply to banks. [S:f41a543388bc, para 41]
- VA management will have no small-amount exception. It covers any business of managing a VA portfolio for others where the manager makes the investment decisions. [S:01c5c5c4045f, paras 32-33]
- Advice on a portfolio that mixes VAs and securities will still need a VA advisory licence or registration for the VA part. [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 21]
- Once the regimes apply, no one may actively market these services to the Hong Kong public without an SFC licence or registration. [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 70]
- The FSTB and SFC encourage firms to talk early with the SFC, or the HKMA where relevant, before applying. [S:6186c01c6649, para 33]; [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 65]; [S:4a0342268bf2, para 7]

## Talking points

- **To the CCO:** All four regimes now have conclusions, and one bill is targeted for 2026. There are no plans to let existing firms carry on while they apply. [S:c6df52e680de, Reply part (3)]; [S:6186c01c6649, para 31]; [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 63]
- **To business heads:** Each of the four activities will need a licence or registration once its regime starts. VA management has no small-amount exception. [S:01c5c5c4045f, paras 32, 63]
- **To the CEO:** Start dates are not set yet. The Government and SFC will weigh how long the market needs to adjust. [S:6186c01c6649, para 32]; [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 64]
- **To Risk:** Under the dealing regime, the SFC will require client VAs to be held with custodians the SFC regulates. [S:6186c01c6649, para 26]

1. Consultation Conclusions on VA dealing and further consultation on VA advisory and management — FSTB and SFC — 24 Dec 2025 — read paras 3-5, 26, 29-36 and footnotes 9-10 — https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/gateway/EN/consultation/doc?refNo=25CP12
2. Consultation Conclusions: VA Custodian Services — FSTB and SFC — 24 Dec 2025 — read paras 6-16, 41-51 — https://www.fstb.gov.hk/fsb/en/publication/consult/doc/Custodian_consultation_conclusion_e.pdf
3. Consultation Conclusions: VA Advisory and VA Management — FSTB and SFC — 26 May 2026 — read paras 6-12, 21, 32, 56-70 — https://www.fstb.gov.hk/fsb/en/publication/consult/doc/VASPVAMSP_consultation_conclusion_e.pdf
